verdict:
FLAT — no entry, and the binding reason is SIZE, not marks. Blue PARTIALLY OVERTURNED red (7/10). The court was convened on my thesis that TCPC is marked wrong IN OUR FAVOUR; that thesis is NEITHER confirmed NOR refuted, because the external anchor both sides leaned on turns out to be too weak to settle the question in either direction.

BOTH TESTS I SET FOR THE ANCHOR CAME BACK AGAINST RED. (a) PRICE OR FEES: footnote 3 of EX-99.1 states the cash adjustment 'includes estimated seller and transaction expenses' — so the -$57.1M is loss PLUS expenses, exactly red's own change-my-mind #4, which its brief then denied. (b) REPRESENTATIVE OR ADVERSELY SELECTED: the sold strip is the SMALL-POSITION TAIL — 78 names averaging $6.7M against $13.9M retained — so extrapolating an 11.16% haircut onto the 56 retained credits is unsupported. (c) Blue also re-derived the stale-basis correction as ~3.7 points, not ~7: NAV/share fell 6.9% in H1 but that is LEVERED 2.4x, and filed depreciation is $48.3M on ~$1.32B = -3.7% at the ASSET level. So 95%-of-12/31/25 is ~98.7% of 6/30/26 carry for an average asset, implying ~$7M of loss rather than $57M. 'Marks are 11% high book-wide' is UNPROVEN.

THE FINDING THAT STOPS EVERYONE: blue caught a reconciliation failure red missed — EX-99.1 does NOT tie sources and uses. Debt falls $591.6M against $152M of gross proceeds and a $141M cash decline. UNTIL THAT RECONCILES, NO BENCH CAN STATE THE CLEARING PRICE, which is precisely the number my thesis and red's kill both depend on. Mark-adjusted NAV is a RANGE, $4.86-$5.90, not either side's point estimate.

AN INPUT I SUPPLIED WAS WRONG AND THE COURT CORRECTED IT. I fed the bench a 160.3% asset-coverage figure and called the ~6.75%-markdown-to-breach cushion the tightest in the cohort. That was the 6/30/26 balance sheet; POST-SALE the balance sheet is genuinely de-levered at 255% asset coverage. The leverage killer I named does not exist — the transaction removed it. Recording this because the adjudicator's own input was the error.

WHAT ACTUALLY SURVIVES, AND WHY IT IS STILL FLAT: a 17-31% discount (not the 38% headline) to a de-levered balance sheet, a dividend covered ~80-92% (blue rebuilt red's arithmetic: the error was EXPENSE MODELLING, not the denominator — a trim to ~$0.15, not a break), and a +45% ceiling. Real but not exceptional. Against that: $1.34M ADV, which at the desk's own <=1%-of-ADV publishing constraint is ~$13K/day of participation, and an UNDATED bankers' process. Blue's phrase is the ruling — RP_FAIR-adjacent but SUB-SCALE AND UNOWNABLE AT THE DESK'S SIZE. A position we cannot build or exit is not a position, however right the thesis.

THE MARK-INTEGRITY LEGS STAND UNREFUTED and keep their value as COHORT knowledge even though the name is flat: TCPC is the cohort's harshest recogniser (non-accruals at 19.4c vs FSK 47.9c, MFIC 55.1c), its incentive-fee hurdle has been unmet since 2013 so zero fee accrues, its PIK fell 48% while NMFC's and FSK's rose, and it carries the contested Kellermeyer credit at 7.2c against FSK's 98.4c accruing. None of that was contradicted; it simply cannot be monetised in this vehicle.
reopen_gates: Q3 10-Q ONLY, and BOTH: (i) retained-book depreciation < 3% AND (ii) Q3 repurchases >= $10M now that coverage permits them.

SOURCES-AND-USES RECONCILIATION (8-K/A or the Q3 10-Q): debt -$591.6M vs $152M gross proceeds and a $141M cash decline do not tie. No clearing price is stateable until it does — this is the finding that blocks BOTH the bull and the bear case, and it is now the PRIMARY reason for FLAT.

A DATED catalyst. 'No specific timetable' on the bankers' process is not one, and the markdown may not be finished (NAV 9.18->6.58 over five quarters) — value-ladder flow gate: do not bid into a markdown still in progress.
The mark-integrity legs (19.4c recognition, zero incentive fee since 2013, PIK -48%) are RETAINED AS COHORT SCREENING KNOWLEDGE, not a TCPC entry case.
adjudicator_note: Adjudicator's own input corrected by the court: I supplied 160.3% asset coverage (6/30/26) and called the cushion the cohort's tightest; post-sale it is 255% and de-levered. The named leverage killer does not exist.
size_gate_RETRACTED_20260817: RETRACTED — I wrote a size gate into this verdict and it was WRONG, on a number I did not check. The blue bench asserted $1.34M ADV and concluded 'sub-scale and unownable at the desk's size'; I repeated it. IBKR's live 90-day average USD volume is $3,441,647 — 2.6x higher. At 1% of ADV that is $34.4k/day: a $50k position (4.9% of the $1.03M book) builds in 1.5 sessions and exits in 1.5, on a 0.49% spread (2c on $4.08) = ~1% round-trip. A +45% move on $50k is $22.5k = 2.2% of NLV. TCPC is comfortably ownable at our size. WORSE, THE OBJECTION CONTRADICTS OUR OWN THESIS: the office thesis says our edge IS the capacity ceiling — we deliberately buy paper institutions cannot, and 'too small for us' should be a near-impossible objection for a $1M book. The bench applied an institutional frame and I did not blue-team it. Note also that the <=1%-of-ADV rule is the RADICAL-HONESTY PUBLISHING constraint (do not move a name we publish ladders on), not a general position limit — so even 1% is conservative for an unpublished position. FLAT STANDS, on the unreconciled sources-and-uses and the absence of a dated catalyst. It does NOT stand on liquidity.
METRIC_INVALIDATION_20260818: *** METRIC INVALIDATED 2026-08-18 (OBDC blue bench) — READ BEFORE USING ANY 'IMPLIED MARK ON NON-ACCRUALS' FIGURE IN THIS RECORD. *** The cohort ladder I built and used all session — TCPC 19.4c / OTF 22.8c / OBDC 29.5c / PNNT 31.1c / FSK 47.9c / WHF 50.4c / MFIC 55.1c — DOES NOT MEASURE MARKING DISCIPLINE. Implied mark = non-accrual FV% / cost% is dominated by CONCENTRATION AND TIMING: it tells you WHEN a manager's worst credit blew up, not how honestly it marks. Proof: 79% of OBDC's entire Q2 unrealized loss is ONE second lien (Loparex, $130.6M marked 63c -> 5c, independently confirmed via PitchBook). Ex-that-single-name OBDC computes at 38.7c rather than 29.5c. A manager whose big blow-up is RECENT looks harsh; one whose blow-up was years ago and is already written to zero looks soft — with identical discipline. THE LADDER MUST BE RECOMPUTED EX-LARGEST-NAME BEFORE IT IS EVER USED TO ORDER MANAGERS AGAIN, and until then no verdict may rest on it. Note the ordering may survive — ex-Loparex OBDC still marks harsher than FSK, WHF and MFIC as published — but that is unproven for the others because only OBDC has been decomposed. Affected: every classification below that cites the ladder, and the court contexts for MFIC, OTF and OBDC.
